notes: The experiment manipulates gelsemine as nectar defence and measures both nectar robbers and pollinators. Total pollinator visits are numerically recovered for both years; 2004 is the natural-range primary effect. Residence/proportion probed and pollen analogue remain separate outcomes.

Useful concentration-dependent pollinator-response study, but the source establishes secondary-compound defence mainly for vegetative tissues and does not itself verify the flower-specific antagonist-reduction role of each nectar compound.

The nectar phenolics strongly reject mismatched visitors but effective bird pollinators are seemingly unaffected. This is a strict-role counterexample to universal pollinator interference and is retained as contextual evidence, not a negative-effect pool entry.

Five dependent assay effects are recovered from source-reported t statistics. Equal-sugar assays show less use of higher-gelsemine flowers, while increasing sugar in the higher-gelsemine option removes the preference difference. All assays remain one study cluster.

The source shows nectar repellents reduce ant visitation and alter pollinator use, while nicotine is an efficient herbivore defence. Visit number and residence/removal can move in opposite directions, so compounds and outcomes remain separated.

The primary source explicitly frames the tested phenolics as defensive plant compounds and reports a nonlinear bee response. Floral/nectar context and exact effect/uncertainty still need to be fixed before pool eligibility.

Manipulated gelsemine reduced pollination and female reproduction while measuring nectar robbing in the same system. It supports the biological conflict but does not belong in preference or visitation-rate pools.

Visit-number effects are recovered separately at 0.1, 1, 2 and 4 microgram per microlitre versus control. The 0.1 contrast is near zero and higher-dose contrasts are increasingly negative; dose rows remain one study cluster.

Natural-range concentrations of most tested compounds did not deter bumblebees; deterrence generally emerged above natural ranges. Do not blanket-code all compounds as B because they are called toxins.

The study states milkweed cardenolides are herbivore defences, manipulates nectar cardenolides, measures mutualist bees and antagonist monarchs, and reports colony-level bee deterrence plus reduced monarch oviposition. Individual-bout and colony-level responses must remain separate.
Useful only if the focal compound independently satisfies the flower-specific antagonist-reduction role; preserve microbe interaction.

Strong strict-B source: Aconitum nectar alkaloids deter robbers at lower concentrations and pollinator visitation declines with alkaloid concentration. Field B-to-P is observational, so it is not pooled with manipulation lnRR.
Numerical preference effects are recovered from source-reported t and df, but the focal experiment does not itself establish a flower-specific antagonist-reduction role for nicotine.
Natural-range effects are weak/species-specific, whereas 1000 ng/uL strongly reduces use in multiple species. Bee species are dependent effects within one study cluster.
Secondary-metabolite status alone is insufficient for B; currently retain outside primary B-to-P pool.
Within the natural milkweed range, low ouabain can increase preference/consumption whereas high ouabain reduces consumption over time. Supporting CSV is the preferred numerical route.

source_locator: Pollen alkaloids are unrelated to pollen-thief abundance, negatively associated with bacterial abundance, and associated with more visits but fewer flowers probed per visit; total flowers visited is unchanged. Do not promote to strict B solely from proposed antimicrobial interpretation.

notes: Potential filtering/specialization case; do not pool until the legitimate-pollinator role and defence role are explicit for each consumer.
